answer: Reputation systems resist sybil attacks by requiring each identity to build verifiable history before gaining influence. An attacker cannot mine a glacier of trust overnight because endorsements must trace to prior contributions. Like copper that conducts only when properly forged, an identity earns weight through continuous honest participation. A juniper bush looks dense but each branch has distinct roots. Networks reject identities appearing fully formed without history, forcing attackers to spend real time building genuine track records before their nodes matter.
